headline: PM Tarique Rahman inaugurates July Uprising Memorial Museum
summary: The museum was established to preserve the memories of the 2024 July mass uprising.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has officially inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum. The facility is dedicated to preserving the history and memories of the July 2024 mass uprising.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by various dignitaries and officials. The museum aims to serve as a permanent record of the events that unfolded during the uprising.
caption:
A new museum opens to preserve the legacy of the 2024 July uprising.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has officially inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum. The facility is dedicated to preserving the history and memories of the July 2024 mass uprising.

The inauguration ceremony was attended by various dignitaries and officials. The museum aims to serve as a permanent record of the events that unfolded during the uprising.

headline_marked: India says [[no involvement in Sheikh Hasina's media event]]
headline: India says no involvement in Sheikh Hasina's media event
summary: The Indian government denies any role in the deposed PM's virtual appearance, while Bangladesh urges local media not to broadcast her speeches.
details: India's external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that a scheduled virtual appearance by deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is being organized by a private media entity and the government has no involvement or endorsement of the views expressed.

The Bangladesh government has urged local media outlets not to publish or broadcast Hasina's speeches, with Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman warning of action against those who violate court orders.

Prime Minister's Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir previously requested India's cooperation to ensure Hasina or Awami League associates are not allowed to use Indian territory for political speeches aimed at creating instability in Bangladesh.
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi assured that the matter would be considered appropriately and that the Indian side would remain vigilant.
Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman also described Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh as 'part of a package,' though he did not elaborate on the details of that package.

Regarding geopolitical challenges, Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government is maintaining discussions with the United States, Russia, Iran, China, and India, and is not facing any significant geopolitical pressure.
